artifacts.notes: The work occupies one wiki page, current revision 263972 at retrieval, which is the glosses on Jerome's prologue and the commentary entire.
artifacts.rights_basis: Remigius of Auxerre's Latin is of the ninth century and Migne's printing is of 1853, so the text beneath these bytes is in the public domain everywhere. The bytes themselves are the wiki source of a Latin Wikisource transcription, and Latin Wikisource contributions are licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 — a condition on the contributors' markup rather than on Migne's text under it. The exact bytes are therefore hashed and recorded but not retained here, and only the printed Latin reaches the tracked derivative, stripped of every template, link, heading and column marker the contributors and the encoder added.

edition.notes: Migne divides the glosses into capita answering to the chapters of Genesis and heads each with `Vers. 5.`, the printing's own statement of the verse glossed. The caput marker for Genesis 5 and for Genesis 50 is missing from the printing, and at Genesis 43 the running head prints a bare `XLIII.` over a lemma that is Genesis 42:1, so the printed markers are checked against the lemma rather than believed. No English translation of this work exists at all.

work.description: A schoolmaster's commentary on the whole of Genesis: short glosses, one to a phrase, explaining a word, a Hebrew name, a difficulty or a figure, and moving on. It opens on Jerome's prologue rather than on Genesis 1, because the prologue is what a reader of the Vulgate meets first, and it runs to the last verse of Genesis 50.
